name: A Review of Prominent Paradigms for LLM-Based Agents: Tool Use (Including RAG), Planning, and Feedback Learning
venue: CoLing 2025 (Proceedings of the 31st International Conference on Computational Linguistics, pp. 9760-9779); preprint arXiv:2406.05804 (submitted Jun 2024, v6 Nov 2024)
authors_affiliation: Xinzhe Li (single author). Independent Researcher; part of the work conducted while affiliated with Deakin University, Australia.
code_url: N/A (no executable code; this is a survey. A maintained reading-list repository is provided instead, see maintained_repo_url)
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/xinzhel/LLM-Agent-Survey (reading list / paper list; ~505 stars; last major update 14 Mar 2025; author announced inactive maintenance from Apr 2025, redirecting to https://github.com/xinzhel/LLM-Search)
task_domain: Survey/taxonomy of LLM-based agents spanning tool use (including RAG), planning, and feedback learning. Covers task domains: QA / NLP-as-agent (NLIE-QA), planning, tool-use, embodied, web, code, and decision-making.
problem_setting: A unified conceptual taxonomy paper (no new empirical method). It defines task environments (decision-making vs Natural Language Interaction Environments/NLIEs), three task-agnostic LLM-Profiled Roles (LMPRs): policy models (actor/planner), evaluators, and dynamic models, and four universal LMPR-based workflows (base, tool-use, search, feedback-learning). Covers single-agent settings, both offline/static (RAG over a corpus) and interactive (search/feedback) workflows. Supervision-wise it discusses prompting (zero-/few-shot) profiling rather than training. RAG is framed as the canonical 'passive tool use' case where a retrieval mechanism collects relevant information to assist the policy model.
what_is_retrieved: As a taxonomy: docs/passages (for RAG-style passive tool use), tools/APIs (for autonomous tool use), and few-shot demonstrations (for prompting LMPRs). The survey treats RAG-retrieved documents/passages as the primary retrieval target; no single retrieved unit is the paper's own contribution.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus. The survey frames RAG-style retrieval as collecting relevant information from an external store given a query (Lewis et al. 2020); it does not center on growing/episodic agent-written memory. [uncertain] (growing memory is not an organizing axis of this survey)
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Not analyzed as a dimension. The survey treats RAG abstractly as 'a retrieval mechanism collects relevant information'; it does not distinguish fixed top-k ranking vs complete-set recovery vs precision-driven variable-size selection. [uncertain]
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (the survey does not adopt a case-based-reasoning framing; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain cycle is discussed)
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. Its organizing concepts are LLM-Profiled Roles (policy/evaluator/dynamic) and universal workflows; feedback-learning workflows (Reflexion, Self-Refine, CRITIC) realize revise-like mechanisms but are not described as CBR.
retrieval_unit: document/passage (for the RAG-style passive tool-use category) and tool/API (for the autonomous tool-use category). At the prompting level, the few-shot demonstration is also a retrievable/selectable unit. The survey does not commit to a single granularity; it describes RAG as retrieving 'relevant information' to assist the policy model.
index_source: Static external corpus (RAG over an external knowledge store). The survey does not analyze offline-induced vs online/test-time-induced stores as an axis. [uncertain]
index_structure_topology: Not analyzed. The survey abstracts RAG as a generic 'retrieval mechanism' and does not categorize index structures (flat vector / graph / hierarchical / cluster). [uncertain]
retriever_type: Not specified as a contribution. RAG is described generically (Lewis et al. 2020); the survey does not taxonomize retriever types (BM25/dense/learned/LLM-as-retriever/generative). [uncertain]
retriever_learning_signal: Not analyzed. The retrieval mechanism in RAG-style passive tool use is treated as off-the-shelf/external; the survey does not discuss how the retriever is trained or selected. [uncertain]
query_construction: The query is the user input/question for RAG-style passive tool use ('given a query, a retrieval mechanism collects relevant information'). For autonomous tool use, tool invocation is triggered by in-generation triggers, the reasoning-acting strategy, or confidence-based invocation rather than an explicit query construction step.
query_granularity: Task-level / one-shot for passive RAG (retrieve from the query). For autonomous tool use (e.g., Active RAG / ReAct), retrieval/tool-calls can occur at the step level during reasoning. The survey distinguishes passive (one-shot at the policy input) from autonomous (interleaved) but does not formalize query granularity beyond this.
when_to_retrieve: The survey distinguishes passive (one-shot: RAG-style, retrieve-then-generate) from autonomous (iterative/active: tool/retrieval invocation triggered during reasoning). It explicitly cites confidence-based invocation (Active RAG, Jiang et al. 2023) as an uncertainty-triggered/active variant.
retrieval_trigger_signal: For RAG-style passive tool use: fixed (retrieve given the query). For autonomous tool use the survey enumerates three concrete trigger mechanisms: (1) in-generation triggers (agent program monitors token generation and pauses on a detected tool trigger), (2) reasoning-acting strategy (ReAct: each reasoning/acting step is a full inference cycle ending with a stop token), and (3) confidence-based invocation (token-confidence-triggered retrieval, used by Active RAG; noted as unable to specify which tool to invoke).
reranking: Not discussed. The survey does not cover reranking stages for retrieved content. [uncertain]
retrieved_context_refinement: Not discussed as a survey axis. RAG-style retrieval is summarized as 'collect relevant information ... to assist generation' with no post-retrieval refinement (rerank/distill/compress/decompose) taxonomy. [uncertain]
tool_document_engineering: Partially noted: for autonomous tool use, the survey states LLMs 'must be aware of the available tools, which requires including tool information during LLM profiling,' and that triggers are defined through tool descriptions and/or few-shot demonstrations. It does not taxonomize tool-document engineering (synthetic-query augmentation / weighted-field embeddings / instruction-tuned tool embeddings).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Not discussed. The survey predates/omits MCP and live tool-index synchronization; tool invocation is described at the workflow/prompting level (in-generation triggers, reasoning-acting), not via a specific integration protocol (RapidAPI/REST/MCP). [uncertain]
tool_dependency_awareness: Not discussed. The survey does not model inter-tool dependencies (output-of-A feeds B, shared auth, prerequisites). [uncertain]
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: retrieved information/tool outputs are integrated into the policy model's context to assist response/decision generation. For passive RAG the retrieved info conditions a single generation; for autonomous tool use, tool outputs are 'integrated into the reasoning process' step by step. No training-signal or latent-token injection is part of the framing.
planning_integration: The survey's central contribution is positioning retrieval/tool-use relative to planning via LMPR-based workflows: (a) RAG-style passive tool use = retrieve-then-generate at the policy input; (b) autonomous tool use = per-step interleaved (in-generation triggers / reasoning-acting / confidence-based) within the policy's rollout; (c) separately, planning is handled by search workflows (Traversal/Heuristic and Simulation-based/MCTS) using policy + evaluator (+ dynamic model). Retrieval is classified under the tool-use paradigm rather than embedded inside the search tree.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Two modes are distinguished: per-answer (passive RAG: one retrieval then generation) vs per-reasoning/acting-step or per-tool-call within a rollout (autonomous tool use: ReAct-style step cycles, in-generation token-monitored triggers, confidence-based per-step invocation).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no CBR case-adaptation framing). For feedback-learning workflows the analogous mechanism is LLM revision conditioned on evaluator/tool/human feedback (e.g., Reflexion, Self-Refine, CRITIC), but the survey describes this as feedback learning, not case adaptation.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw retrieved text/information injected into the prompt (for RAG) and raw tool outputs integrated into reasoning (for autonomous tool use). The survey does not analyze distilled-strategy / executable-skill / latent-token representations.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: For RAG-style passive tool use: raw retrieved information/document content (low abstraction). For prompting LMPRs: single demonstrations (few-shot). The survey does not analyze higher-abstraction retrieved units (distilled strategy / workflow / procedural skill).
noise_robustness_mechanism: Not discussed. The survey does not cover retriever-aware training, relevance evaluators, or distractor filtering for retrieved context (though feedback-learning workflows provide a general self-correction/validation mechanism, e.g., CRITIC validating outputs with tools). [uncertain]
memory_type: none (workflow/role taxonomy). The survey organizes agents by LLM-Profiled Roles and workflows, not by a memory store. Feedback-learning workflows (e.g., Reflexion) maintain self-reflection text across trials, but the survey does not formalize this as a retrievable memory type.
write_back: False at the survey level. No memory write-back is an organizing dimension. (Reflexion-style verbal feedback retained across trials is mentioned within the feedback-learning paradigm but not framed as memory write-back.)
online_growth: False / not an axis. The survey does not analyze whether a retrievable store grows during deployment. [uncertain]
write_back_trigger: N/A (no memory write-back framing in this taxonomy). Within feedback-learning workflows the analogous trigger is reflective (after evaluator self-critique) and can use both success and failure signals, but the survey does not formalize a write-back trigger.
failure_experience_usage: Not formalized. The feedback-learning paradigm covered (Reflexion, Self-Refine, CRITIC) uses evaluator/tool/environment feedback (including failure signals) to revise decisions, but the survey does not analyze success-only vs success+failure storage of experiences. [uncertain]
retrieval_as_learned_policy: False. The survey treats retrieval (RAG) as an external/off-the-shelf mechanism and tool invocation as prompt-driven (trigger/reasoning-acting/confidence); it does not frame retrieval/case-selection as a learned or RL-optimized policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A. The survey focuses on single-agent, task-agnostic workflows (its unifying value is cross-FRAMEWORK comparison of LMPRs/workflows, but not shared memory/experience across agents). No cross-agent memory sharing is discussed.
benchmarks: No experiments are run by this survey. It catalogs environments/benchmarks used by reviewed frameworks, including: Game of 24 / CrossWords, Blocksworld (BlocksWorld), AlfWorld, VirtualHome, Minecraft, Webshop, WebArena, AppWorld, GSM8K, HotpotQA. (Repo benchmark section also lists MetaTool, TaskBench, PlanBench.)
benchmark_family: Mixed (catalog only): embodied (ALFWorld/VirtualHome/Minecraft), web (Webshop/WebArena/AppWorld), QA / multi-hop (GSM8K/HotpotQA), rule-based games/planning (Game of 24/Blocksworld). The survey reports no metrics of its own.
baselines: N/A (survey; no empirical comparison). It compares COVERAGE against four highly-cited surveys (Guo et al. 2024; Xi et al. 2023; Huang et al. 2024; Wang et al. 2024a) along tool-use / planning / feedback-learning / universal-LMPR axes (Table 1), not method baselines.
key_metrics: N/A (survey; reports no quantitative metrics). The only quantitative comparison is a qualitative coverage matrix (checkmarks/crosses with section pointers) against prior surveys.
headline_result: N/A (no empirical headline number). The headline contribution is the unified taxonomy: three task-agnostic LLM-Profiled Roles (policy/evaluator/dynamic models) and four universal workflows (base, tool-use, search, feedback-learning) enabling cross-paradigm comparison, plus identification of three limitations of existing workflow designs.
evaluation_decoupling: N/A. No retrieval or task metrics are reported; the survey reports neither intrinsic retrieval metrics nor end-to-end task metrics.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: N/A (no metrics reported). Conceptually the survey emphasizes process/workflow structure (how LMPRs interact) over outcomes, but it does not score either.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Not quantified. The survey discusses qualitative workflow trade-offs (e.g., search/MCTS planning complexity, the cost of deliberate multi-step NLIE design) but reports no retrieval-call counts, API cost, latency, or token-saving numbers. [uncertain]
context_budget_and_selection_count: Not discussed. No token budget or top-k selection analysis. [uncertain]
survey_scope_and_axes: Organizing axes: (1) task universality (decision-making environments: rule-based games, embodied; vs information-processing environments: web, NLIEs); (2) three task-agnostic LLM-Profiled Roles (LMPRs): policy models (actor/planner), evaluators, dynamic models; (3) four universal LMPR-based workflows: base, tool-use (RAG-style passive / passive validation / autonomous / autonomous validation), search (traversal & heuristic / simulation-based MCTS), feedback-learning (from evaluator only / evaluator+task-env / humans); (4) cross-paradigm discussion and three identified limitations. Reference count: 59 references. Coverage window: work through ~2024 (CoLing 2025 camera-ready, extended to 9 pages); maintained repo extends to ~Mar 2025.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (this is a survey, not a benchmark; it constructs no dataset).
builds_on: Foundational frameworks it unifies: ReAct (Yao et al. 2023b), CoT (Wei et al. 2022), Tree-of-Thoughts (Yao et al. 2023a), RAP (Hao et al. 2023), Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023), Self-Refine (Madaan et al. 2023), CRITIC (Gou et al. 2024), RAG (Lewis et al. 2020), Active RAG (Jiang et al. 2023), LLM-MCTS, AgentQ. Conceptually builds on RL formalisms (policy/evaluator/dynamic model; MDP).
contrasts_with: Explicitly positioned against four prior surveys (Table 1): Guo et al. (2024), Xi et al. (2023), Huang et al. (2024, planning-focused), and Wang et al. (2024a) -- criticizing them for focusing on a single paradigm/domain or lacking a unified comparison basis; notes Wang et al. (2024a) discuss LLM profiling only as personas, not as general roles. Also contrasts task-agnostic 'workflows' against task-specific 'frameworks'.
lineage: Surveys group. A cross-cutting taxonomy survey that bridges tool use (with RAG framed as passive tool use), planning, and feedback learning under unified LLM-Profiled Roles -- bridging groups B (planning/search), C (tool use/RAG), and E (feedback learning / self-correction). Companion to the author's later TMLR 2025 search survey (LLM Test-Time Compute via Search).
